issue.title: sase memory list reports the literal placeholder sase/memory/<web>.md as two missing references
issue.description:
Run `sase memory list` from a sase workspace (checkout 1765b289be, 2026-10-05). The
"Context Files" table shows two `missing` rows:

- `sase/memory/<web>.md`  ← referenced by `AGENTS.md`
- `~/sase/memory/<web>.md` ← referenced by `~/AGENTS.md`

The summary panel counts them as "Missing references 2".

Root cause: `_MEMORY_PATH_RE` in `src/sase/memory/inventory_references.py:25-27`
(`(?:sase/)?memory/[^\s,;:()[\]{}"'`/]+?\.md`) accepts `<` and `>`. As a result it
matches the literal placeholder text `sase/memory/<web>.md`, which
`src/sase/main/init_memory/templates/memory-sase.template.md:9` inlines into every
generated AGENTS.md (the Memory webs bullet). The same text also appears in
`memory-README.template.md:16`.

Fix direction: exclude `<`/`>` from the path character class (or skip matches that
contain angle-bracket placeholders), and add a regression test that runs the
generated sase.md text through the reference parser.

task_type_fields.impact: Every `sase memory list` run reports two false missing references, so the missing count is never zero. That hides real missing memory references among the noise.
